elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and Customer's affiliates against every category of covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.1.1 and 12.1.3 require SFJ to indemnify and hold harmless, but no operative language requires SFJ to defend PB or its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and Customer's affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 indemnifies the PB Indemnified Parties, including PB and its Affiliates, against third-party claims alleging infringement or misappropriation caused by SFJ's performance or materials, technology, or methods supplied by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and Customer's affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No SFJ indemnity trigger expressly covers SFJ's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and Customer's affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No SFJ indemnity trigger addresses a data breach, security incident, or unauthorized disclosure caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and Customer's affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.1(a) covers third-party claims arising from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of SFJ, its Affiliates, and their Permitted Third Parties in performing SFJ's obligations.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: Section 12.2.1 requires prompt written notice and expressly applies to Section 12.1.3; late notice relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent of actual prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language contains no defense-control or settlement-control provision.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 12.2.1 requires delivery of papers and official documents, but does not impose a general reasonable-cooperation or assistance obligation.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: The rendered PB indemnity does not expressly establish a Customer-provided-content indemnity.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor against third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered PB indemnity refers to material breach of the agreements and protocols, not PB's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Customer must have no indemnity obligations outside claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: PB remains responsible for additional categories, including contractual and protocol breaches, Product or PB-performance infringement, subject injuries, clinical-trial claims, and commercialization claims.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and Customer's affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor's services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 covers the PB Indemnified Parties against third-party claims alleging infringement or misappropriation by SFJ's contractual performance or supplied materials, technology, or methods.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude infringement arising from modifications made by or for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 expressly excludes infringement arising from modifications made by or for PB.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude infringement arising from combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 expressly excludes combinations of the affected item with items not supplied by SFJ.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude infringement arising from specifications furnished by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 expressly excludes infringement arising from specifications furnished by PB.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to procure Customer's continued right to use an affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 requires SFJ to procure for PB the right to continue using the affected item as one remedial option.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to modify an affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 permits SFJ to modify the affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to replace an affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 permits SFJ to replace the affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must refund amounts paid for the affected item if procurement, modification, and replacement are not commercially reasonable.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 requires a refund of amounts paid for the affected item if the preceding remedies are not commercially reasonable.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.3 limits aggregate liability to three times the amounts paid or payable in the preceding twelve months, with a floor based on three times the first twelve months' amounts. The operative wording uses annual amounts rather than the word “fees,” but establishes the required 3× annualized super-cap structure.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by adding the SFJ IP indemnity, all three customary exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a 3× twelve-month super-cap. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits a defense duty, breach-of-law and Vendor-caused data-breach coverage, defense control, and general cooperation, while PB's indemnity remains substantially broader than Customer-provided content and breach of law. It is not minimal because it also narrows PB's existing IP indemnity and adds a first-year cap floor not required to complete the fallback. The cap sentence is also internally awkward: it states that SFJ's “aggregate liability” both will not exceed one amount and will in no event be less than another, potentially creating conflicting maximum and minimum liability rather than clearly flooring the cap.
